sections.label: Bots and AVAs
sections.title: Who chooses the next step?
sections.lead: Agentic means choosing the next permitted action, not just generating a more natural answer.

comparisonTable.label: Digital bots and Agentic Virtual Agents
comparisonTable.overview: People remain in control in both approaches.

rows.cue: The difference is where the sequencing decision sits.
An AVA uses the current context and tool results to choose its next step.
Neither approach can change policy or grant itself permission.

comparisonTable.takeaway: Both can use natural language and call APIs. The difference is who chooses what happens next.

sections.note: Start simple. Introduce agentic reasoning when the journey needs it.

sections.label: 01 Gifted funds
sections.title: One question becomes two.
sections.lead: Gifted funds and a bank connection that will not complete.

dialogue.speaker: Homebuyer
dialogue.text: My parents are helping with my deposit, and my bank will not connect.

dialogue.speaker: Support journey
dialogue.text: Clarify the gift, understand the bank issue, then guide an approved next step.

sections.takeaway: Bot: standard guidance. AVA: joins the two needs and adapts. Human: evidence or policy judgement.
sections.note: Help with the process. Do not approve the funds.

sections.label: 04 Message reassurance

items.title: An expected check
items.body: Use approved guidance. Confirm with the requesting firm through trusted contact details.

items.title: Unexpected or suspicious
items.body: Stop and reach trusted support. Do not treat a message or link as proof.

items.title: A strong simple-bot journey
items.body: No AVA is needed for the standard answer. Suspected fraud goes straight to a person.

sections.question: What reassurance is safe before identity is confirmed?

sections.label: Choose the first proof
sections.title: Which journey should we prove first?
sections.lead: Pick one high-volume simple journey and one complex exception.

items.title: Where is the volume?
items.body: Top contact reasons, repeat contacts and current friction.

items.title: What can we safely access?
items.body: Approved knowledge, status data, actions and handoff rules.

items.title: What would success look like?
items.body: Task completion, repeat contact and cost per resolved enquiry.

sections.question: Agree the outcome first. Then build the demo around it.
